en: The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara from the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-dhāraṇī-mahātantrarāja*,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao-san Dafu, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

I now take refuge in the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. I shall briefly describe the ritual of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, The great King of Tantras corresponding to that [teaching], Which is capable of accomplishing all deeds for the benefit of sentient beings.
At that time, the World-Honored One...
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, he expounded the great teachings corresponding to the Buddhas.
The Buddha said: "If the ācārya and the practitioner..."
Those who wish to practice the factors of enlightenment (bodhipakṣadharma) and various accomplishments should cultivate the dharma of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
If one practices this dharma, one should first seek a quiet place.
Relying upon the ritual procedures with single-minded diligence and without slackening,
one should cultivate the preliminary practices until they are thoroughly mastered;
thereafter, according to the dharma, one performs the visualization and recites the syllable HŪṂ.
Having selected the site, performed the rite of delimiting the boundary, and expelled the māras,
the practitioner of recitation then spreads grass upon that spot and sits down.
At that time, the reciter—
When one intends to direct the mind toward the visualization of the worthy ones and the sages,
one must first purify the three karmas. Thereupon,
recite the mantra for purifying the three karmas as follows:
Oṃ karyavakubhañjita vajrasphoṭakaḥ. Having recited this mantra, [proceed].
Furthermore, it is said in a verse of simile:
"Just as a pure and wondrously colored lotus, Though born from within the mud, cannot be defiled by it;
So too do sentient beings dwelling amidst afflictions Attain complete purity within the three realms."
Having recited the gāthā,
one should visualize that upon one's own crown is a jeweled tiara,
within which resides Amitāyus Buddha.
Next, one should visualize a fully blossomed white lotus emerging from the heart;
upon that flower, visualize a lunar disc;
and within the lunar disc, visualize the syllable Oṃ appearing.
The essence is like space, consisting solely of true great wisdom.
Then, recite the mantra for opening wisdom:
Oṃ jñānapratividdhe 'ṅkari me. Having recited this mantra, [proceed].
Again, visualize that the various jewels transform into an eight-petaled lotus.
Above that flower, visualize a lunar disc.
Within the lunar disc, the syllable *hrīṃ* appears.
This is the very form of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara himself,
seated in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*), his body red in color and possessing two arms.
To the left of the Bodhisattva, one should visualize the Bodhisattva Pāṇḍaravāsinī.
Holding a lotus flower in hand,
next visualize the sages and worthies of the eight directions.
First, at the position of the eastern petal of the lotus:
Visualize yourself as the Bodhisattva Vairocanī,
holding a red lotus flower.
The mantra of the Bodhisattva is as follows:
Oṃ vilokini avalokaya svāhā. At the position of the southern petal of the lotus, visualize the Bodhisattva Tārā appearing there.
Holding a green lotus in hand, the Bodhisattva’s mantra is:
Oṃ tarī tārī ture svāhā. Next, at the position of the western petal of the lotus.
Visualize the Bodhisattva Pūrṇa holding an utpala flower,
within which is an eight-spoked wheel.
The mantra of the Bodhisattva is:
Oṃ burini mahācakravartini hūṃ. Next, at the position of the northern petal of the lotus.
Visualize the Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī holding a yellow lotus.
The mantra of the Bodhisattva is as follows:
Oṃ bṛkuti tati mata hūṃ. Then, at the position of the northeastern petal of the lotus, one should visualize the Bodhisattva Padmavāsini.
Holding a crimson lotus in her hand, the mantra of the Bodhisattva is:
Oṃ mahāśrīye maṇipadme hūṃ. Next, at the position of the southeastern petal of the lotus:
Visualize oneself as the Bodhisattva Vajrapadmaśrī, holding a white lotus flower in hand.
The mantra of this Bodhisattva is as follows:
Oṃ vajrapadmīśvarī dhāra padmī hūṃ. First, at the position of the southwestern petal of the lotus.
One should visualize the Bodhisattva Padma appearing at the tail,
holding a black lotus. The mantra of the Bodhisattva is as follows:
Oṃ viśvapadmahrīḥ. First, at the position of the northwest petal of the lotus, visualize the Bodhisattva Viśvavajra appearing.
Holding a *karmavajra* in hand, the mantra of the Bodhisattva is:
Oṃ viśvavajri hūṃ. First, [place it] at the center of the lotus.
Again, one should visualize the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara manifesting a great and wondrous form-body.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ hrīṃ padmanarteśvara hūṃ. Such are the mantras of these great bodhisattvas and their subtle, wondrous mantras.
If a practitioner of recitation performs the visualization according to the ritual and recites the mantra with single-minded concentration without regressing,
this person shall swiftly realize the fruit of Buddhahood in the future.
Even while experiencing the pleasures of the five desires,
one is able to fulfill the ten pāramitās and the gates of dhāraṇī,
up to the states of the pratyekabuddhas, the ten stages of the bodhisattvas, and the state of the Buddha’s tranquility.
One will swiftly attain accomplishment; do not give rise to doubt.
Furthermore, the practitioner who maintains the recitation must also constantly consume the five kinds of Mahāyāna medicines.
That is to say:
if one can constantly consume such medicines as ṛddhijitakalparājakṛtasaṃjñānavajrodana and so forth, [one will attain the desired results].
Furthermore, by reciting [the mantra] without ceasing,
one will swiftly be freed from the sufferings of old age and illness, increase one's lifespan,
transform one's physical appearance so that all who see it feel love and respect, and attain these benefits.
In this present life, one shall attain supreme wisdom.
Furthermore, all rites for pacification, enrichment, magnetizing, and subjugation—
up to and including summoning, the eradication of all māras, and dispatching them away— shall be accomplished.
The spells for subjugating enemies and the methods for striking down evildoers,
up to and including the power of moving through the air at will and all various *samādhis*—
if one practices the method of Avalokiteśvara, all these shall be accomplished.
The root mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva is:
Oṃ hrīḥ padmanarteśvara hūṃ. Furthermore, if there is a practitioner who recites it:
If one constantly recollects this root mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and recites it one hundred and eight times every day,
all the transgressions committed by that person during the day and night will be completely extinguished.
If one recites it five hundred times a day,
one can eliminate all illnesses;
if one recites it one thousand times a day, one will obtain an increase in lifespan.
If one recites it two thousand times, one will receive the respect of the multitude.
If one maintains the recitation for three thousand times, the love and respect of the multitude will increase and one’s wealth and status will flourish.
If one maintains the recitation for four thousand times, one will be freed from poverty and suffering.
If one recites it five thousand times, it can cause the bodies and minds of all enemies to become agitated and confused.
If one recites it six thousand times, one can subdue all enemies.
If one recites it seven thousand times, one can subdue the four māras.
If one recites it eight thousand times, one can subjugate all devas and devīs;
if one recites it nine thousand times, one can subjugate yakṣas and yakṣīs;
if one recites it ten thousand times, one can subjugate devas, nāgas, and humans.
If one recites it twenty thousand times, the various hidden deities and sages will bring about accomplishment.
If one recites it thirty thousand times, one can fulfill all wishes.
If one recites it forty thousand times, one shall attain the mastery of soaring through the air.
If one recites it fifty thousand times, one shall attain the accomplishment of the sacred sword (*khaḍga-siddhi*).
If one recites it sixty thousand times, one shall become a Vidyādhara.
If one recites it seventy thousand times, one shall become a lord of the world.
If one recites it eighty thousand times, one shall attain the rank of an Iron Wheel-turning King (Cakravartin).
If one recites it ninety thousand times, one shall attain the rank of a Gold Wheel-turning King.
If one recites it one hundred thousand times (lakṣa), one shall attain the rank of a Bodhisattva.
If one recites it ten lakṣas of times, one shall attain mastery and fulfill the ten stages (bhūmis).
If one recites it fifty lakṣas of times, one shall realize the state of Buddhahood.
If one recites it one koṭi of times...
One shall then attain the complete fulfillment of the body, speech, and mind of Amitāyus Buddha in the world of Sukhāvatī,
thereby bringing benefit and happiness to sentient beings.
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke the mantra of the lay bodhisattva, saying:
Oṃ pañcaravasiṃ varade hūṃ. This is the subtle and wondrous mantra of the Bodhisattva Pāṇḍaravāsī.
If a person can constantly recite it, [they shall attain the desired results].
All karmic offenses whatsoever will be completely extinguished.
If one can focus the mind according to the ritual and recite for a full seven days, [the result will be attained].
Within all kingdoms and cities,
all the people will revere and honor them.
If one maintains this recitation for one month, one shall attain great wealth and nobility.
Reciting in this manner until reaching one hundred thousand recitations (lakṣa),
one shall obtain power no different from that of a Bodhisattva.
Furthermore, the mantra of the Bodhisattva Vairocanī is now proclaimed:
Oṃ vairocani avalokaya svāhā. This is the subtle and wondrous mantra of this Bodhisattva.
If a person recites it ten thousand times according to the ritual method, [the desired result will be attained].
One shall attain the accomplishment of the Noble Sword.
If there is any matter for which the reciter has a request,
one should take a tooth-stick and empower it twenty-one times.
He brushes his teeth and goes to sleep;
whatever he seeks, all is explained within his dreams.
All that is spoken is entirely true.
Furthermore, the mantra of the Bodhisattva Tārā is spoken as follows:
Oṃ tārī tud-tārī tur svāhā. This is the subtle and wondrous mantra of this Bodhisattva.
If a person recites this according to the ritual for one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*),
they will be able to summon all the devas, nāgas, asuras, and vidyādharas of the three realms,
as well as their female consorts, to serve as their servants; there shall be none who do not comply with their every wish.
If the practitioner of recitation wishes to summon those devas, nāgas, and their consorts,
they should visualize their bodies as red in color,
with a vajra hook within their hearts.
With blazing radiance, one hooks their heart;
furthermore, one visualizes binding them around the neck with a lasso to produce a state of terror.
Whatever is thus hooked will certainly arrive swiftly, in accordance with the time of recitation.
Whatever one seeks shall be obtained entirely according to one’s heart.
Furthermore, the mantra of the Bodhisattva Pūṇi is proclaimed as follows:
Oṃ pūṇi mahācakravartini hūṃ. This is the subtle and wondrous mantra of this Bodhisattva.
If a person who maintains this recitation seeks accomplishment,
they should first use substances such as vīṇāvaśruṇāga and others to smear the maṇḍala in the shape of a full moon.
Thereafter, one should prepare incense, flowers,
and other offerings according to one's means and perform worship therein.
The practitioner who recites the mantra should then arrange a seat and sit down.
If one recites with single-minded concentration and without ceasing,
whatever one seeks will surely be accomplished, and one shall experience happiness.
After the end of this life, one shall be reborn in the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
Furthermore, the mantra of the Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī is proclaimed as follows:
Oṃ bhr̥kuṭi tsiṭi mṛta hūṃ. This is the subtle and wondrous mantra of this Bodhisattva.
If a person, while reciting [the mantra], wishes to perform a rite of subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*),
they should take earth from beneath the feet of the enemy as well as earth from both banks of a river.
Furthermore, they should use poison, mustard seeds, salt, and blood.
Together with Vināyaka, Vajrīṇa, Naga, and others,
they collectively fashioned clay images of enemies;
using human bone as stakes, they nailed them into the various limbs and joints of the images.
Place it within a skull and cover it with a skull lid.
Heat it over the fire used for cremating corpses in a śmaśāna forest.
Recite the mantra and perform consecration for twenty-one days and nights; it will certainly be subdued.
Furthermore, the mantra of the Bodhisattva Padmavāsini is proclaimed as follows:
Oṃ mahāśrīye maṇipadme hūṃ. This is the subtle and wondrous mantra of this Bodhisattva.
When performing the recitation,
one should first present the five kinds of offerings, such as incense and flowers,
before commencing the recitation.
It can provide protection in all places;
one will achieve definitive victory in philosophical debate and attain great mastery equal to that of Avalokiteśvara.
If one performs homa with ten thousand lotuses, one will become a lord of the earth;
if one performs homa with one lakṣa of lotuses, one will attain the rank of a universal monarch (cakravartin).
Furthermore, the mantra of the Bodhisattva Vajrapadmasarī is proclaimed as follows:
Oṃ vajrapadmī sarī varapadmī hūṃ. This is the subtle and wondrous mantra of this Bodhisattva.
When the practitioner forms a mental intention while reciting,
they are able to subdue and summon;
if they recite seven times, they can protect their own person.
If one recites this one thousand times,
it can eliminate dangers such as poisonous drugs, swords, lions, elephants, snakes, fire, thieves, imprisonment,
and sea-demons; furthermore, it cures diseases such as śleṣman, kṣaya, kuṣṭha, gaṇḍa, vidradhi, and so forth.
Furthermore, it expels all malevolent and venomous beings;
if one recites it one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*),
one's lifespan will increase, and even the aged shall become young again.
His physical marks are perfectly complete, and he is loved and revered by all.
If there is a drought within the realm,
one should select a site in that place and draw a dragon pond.
Then, standing before the pond, one should mentally recite the name of the nāga and perform homa with white mustard seeds and salt;
immediately a great rain will fall, and the entire region will enjoy abundant harvests.
Furthermore, the mantra of the Bodhisattva Viśvapadma is spoken:
Oṃ viśvapadme hrīḥ. This is the subtle and wondrous mantra of this Bodhisattva.
If a person recites with focused concentration,
they shall attain perfection in the actions of body, speech,
and mind, and be able to accomplish various undertakings.
These include the methods for subduing and suppressing demons and malevolent spirits, the method of driving in ritual stakes,
the method of hooking another's mind, the method of illusory transformations,
and even opening the caves of asuras and rendering oneself invisible.
One will be able to accomplish all forms of mastery in traveling through the air.
Furthermore, the mantra of the Bodhisattva Viśvavajra is spoken:
Oṃ viśvavajri hūṃ. This is the subtle and wondrous mantra of this Bodhisattva.
If the practitioner recites with focused diligence according to the ritual,
they will always be able to protect themselves and others,
and shall attain the love and respect of all.
Furthermore, he attains great eloquence that surpasses the eloquence of others.
Moreover, this bodhisattva is able to rescue sentient beings within the realms of hell,
hungry ghosts, and animals, exerting great diligence.
Just as with Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
if there are those who have faith and reverence for the Buddha-dharma,
the Bodhisattva shall always protect them as if they were his own mother.

The Buddha said: "Furthermore, if there be a person who, regarding this King of Great Teachings on the Correspondence with the Gathering of All Tathāgatas, the Ritual Manual for the Recitation of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva..."
With a mind free from doubt and firm in one's practice,
one shall attain the accomplishment of the ultimate Dharma.
Furthermore, there are those who do not enter the maṇḍala.
Even those who possess afflictions and are further lacking in merit may,
according to their own desires, engage in walking, standing, sitting, or staying;
whether speaking or laughing, they do not cease these activities.
Constantly generating the thought of Bodhicitta and contemplating the true principle, one should always maintain the recitation;
all dharmas thus performed will be accomplished.
Furthermore, the person who maintains the recitation shall generate the thought of Bodhicitta.
He partakes of the five kinds of holy medicines, namely the holy medicines known as mahā-ṛkṣa-kalpa-rakta-candana and so forth.
If one recites the mantra according to the ritual manual of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and makes offerings to the worthy sages,
this person need not create an image of the Buddha.
One will also be able to attain the supreme union,
achieve the rank of the Bodhisattva Vajrasattva,
and swiftly realize enlightenment.
What are the signs of such accomplishment?
Those factors conducive to enlightenment (*bodhipākṣika-dharma*), the perfections (*pāramitā*), the gateways of dhāraṇī, the ten stages (*bhūmi*), and so forth, are spontaneously accomplished.
This applies to anyone who is able to rely upon and recite the teachings corresponding to all Buddhas.
This is then no different from all Buddhas.
Furthermore, if the mind of one who recites is not yet tranquil,
they will be unable to comprehend the methods of correspondence.
I shall now explain for them the method for the painted image (*paṭa*).
If a practitioner who maintains the recitation wishes to paint a *paṭa*,
they should first seek out a skillful painter.
First, one should command the purification of body and mind and the observance of the fast (upavāsa).
Then, using a high-quality piece of silk with fringed ends,
measuring two cubits in length, and employing excellent pigments.
On a piece of silk, draw a moon disc;
within the moon disc, draw an eight-petaled lotus of various colors;
and in the center of the flower, draw the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
The body is red in color, with three faces and six arms.
On his crown he wears a jeweled tiara containing Akṣobhya Buddha.
The right face is black and slightly displays a wrathful expression.
The left face is white;
with six arms, he holds a lotus according to the ritual rules.
On the position of the eastern petal, one should paint the Bodhisattva Vairocanī.
The body is white in color;
the left hand holds a red lotus,
and the right hand holds a vajra.
In the south-eastern position, paint the Bodhisattva Tārā;
her body is green in color,
and her left hand holds a green lotus flower.
Holding a jewel in her right hand;
in the position of the western petal, paint the Bodhisattva Pūrṇa,
her body golden in color.
Holding an utpala lotus with a wheel inside it, on the position of the northern petal, one should paint the Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī.
Her body is reddish-white in color; she holds a yellow lotus and a sharp sword.
In the position of the northeastern petal, one should paint the Bodhisattva Padmavāsini;
her body is golden in color,
and she holds a crimson lotus flower in her hand.
In the southeast petal-position, one should paint the Bodhisattva Vajrapadmīśvarī;
her body is the color of space,
and she holds a white lotus and a crystal rosary.
In the southwestern petal-position, one should paint the Bodhisattva Viśvabhadra-padmā;
his body is the color of autumn moonlight,
and he holds a black lotus as well as the Dharma-scriptures.
In the position of the northwest petal, one should paint the Bodhisattva Viśvavajra;
his body is of various colors,
and he holds a lotus flower in his hand outside the petal.
In the four corners, paint the four attendant Bodhisattvas—Mālā, Gītā, Nṛtyā, and Hāsā.
Next, at the positions of the four gates, visualize the four subtle syllables: *Jaṃ*, *Hūṃ*, *Bhrūṃ*, and *Hoḥ*.
They transform into the four bodhisattvas— Aṅkuśa, Pāśa, Śṛṅkhalā, and Ghanta—
who guard the four gates.
Next, the method for painting the images is explained.
As previously described, a skillful painter shall depict the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara upon a plain silk cloth;
his body is the color of autumn moonlight, and he is endowed with all the marks of perfection.
Upon his crown is Amitāyus Buddha.
He has eight arms;
in his first right hand, he holds a rosary.
The second hand holds a jeweled staff;
the third hand holds a trident;
and the fourth hand forms the mudrā of granting boons (varada-mudrā).
The first left hand holds a lotus flower;
the second hand holds a kamaṇḍalu;
the third hand holds a pāśa.
The fourth hand holds the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra;
he wears a tiger-skin garment and has a dragon draped across his chest,
standing or sitting in the full-lotus posture upon a lotus flower.
To the right of the Bodhisattva, depict the practitioner of recitation,
holding an argha vessel and an incense burner,
and assuming an attitude of reverence.
Furthermore, the method for painting an image is explained:
one should paint the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara according to the iconographic conventions of Mount Potalaka.
The body is white in color and possesses the marks of perfection;
she is adorned with white garments and holds a rosary in her right hand.
With his left hand resting on his cheek, he displays the gesture of contemplating the benefit of all sentient beings.
He sits upon a lion-lotus throne;
his left foot hangs down, treading upon a lotus flower.
The right foot rests upon a lotus seat.
Furthermore, the method for painting the image is explained:
as before, [it should be drawn] upon plain silk.
Paint an image of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
with a body of reddish-white color and ten arms.
The right hand first holds a rosary;
the remaining four hands display the gesture of granting fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*) to rescue sentient beings from their hardships.
The left hand first holds a red lotus with two stalks.
Above [his head] is the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra;
his remaining four hands likewise display the gesture of granting fearlessness to rescue sentient beings from their hardships.
He sits upon a lion-lotus throne.
He hangs down his left foot, which is supported by a lotus flower.
On the right side of the Bodhisattva, one should paint a lion, an elephant, fire, and a snake;
on the left side, one should paint bandits, those under restraint, and sea-demons.
When sentient beings encounter these eight difficulties,
he manifests the form of a Bodhisattva to deliver them;
furthermore, he explains the method for painting his image.
As previously described, using plain white silk,
one should paint Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
appearing amidst a lunar disc and manifesting in various colors.
It has thirteen heads,
each adorned with a jeweled crown containing Amitāyus Buddha;
the front face is perfectly full.
The thirteenth face is green and appears upon a horse head;
it has a hundred arms,
holding various implements of ritual action (*karmapātra*).
Alternatively, one may depict [the deity] with a hundred heads and a thousand arms,
likewise holding various implements and weapons of ritual action (*karmapātra*).
All such painted images are as described.
On the right side of each, depict the practitioner performing recitation,
kneeling in the *hu-kuei* posture with reverence,
holding an *argha* bowl, an incense burner, and other such implements.
Regarding the aforementioned various painted images,
the practitioner who performs the recitation should paint one image according to their own preference;
in each case, they must generate a most supreme and distinguished resolve.
Once the painting has been completed,
one should prepare various exquisite incenses, flowers, food, drink, and all manner of ritual implements,
and arrange them before the painting.
Having requested the ācārya to perform the celebratory praise according to the ritual,
the practitioner should then personally purify themselves.
Seated before this painting, they should settle their mind in meditative concentration.
Recite the fundamental, subtle, and wondrous mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
If one remains free from all doubt and distraction, focusing with unwavering diligence,
everything one undertakes will certainly be accomplished.
Furthermore, after the Ācārya has performed the celebratory praise and transmitted the fundamental, subtle, and sublime mantra,
that practitioner of recitation shall perform the rites of a disciple.
One should offer various kinds of rare jewels, gold, silver, and wealth,
even up to one's kingdom, cities, and life itself,
to present to the ācārya as a token of gratitude.
Why is this? Because such dharmas as described above are difficult to encounter, let alone to receive their transmission.
Therefore, with a reverent mind, one should seek an ācārya and pray that he bestow his joy.
Furthermore, this dharma must not be transmitted to those who are not easy [to discipline].
Such persons lack a reverent and devout mind and may fearfully invite evil retribution.

This is the *One-Scroll Ritual for the Recitation of the Holy Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, from the *Mahātantrarāja-sarvabuddhasaṃgīti-sūtra* spoken by the Buddha. Engraved under imperial decree at the Goryeo National Printing Office of the Tripitaka in the year of Yisi (1205).
